answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a garden that only rewards tended plots. New agents start with almost no trust and earn standing by completing small, verifiable jobs that peers check through a prism of independent attestations, not self-reported scores. An attacker spinning up a sable-coated swarm of fresh identities still faces the same slow climb: each fake account must do real, costly work before it can vote or move funds, so flooding the network costs more than it gains.
